title: Monthly WP-CLI Maintenance Round
description: Entry-level monthly pass on a business WordPress site: inspect updates, export the database, update core and plugins, remove a risky File Manager plugin, lock wp-admin installs, flush cache.
instructions: You are on production in /var/www/html. Order matters — look first, back up before updates, harden after. Hints describe the action, not the full command. Type each command in the terminal.

steps.hint: Show which WordPress core version is installed
steps.feedback_wrong: Start with the current core version — you need a baseline.
steps.feedback_correct: Baseline noted. Check whether a core update is available.

steps.hint: Check if WordPress core has an available update
steps.feedback_wrong: Use check-update before you change anything.
steps.feedback_correct: Minor and major are both listed. For this entry round we will take the minor path after a backup.

steps.hint: List only plugins that have an update available
steps.feedback_wrong: Filter the plugin list to updates that are available.
steps.feedback_correct: You can see what will change. Back up the database before any update.

steps.hint: Export the database to a backup file before updates
steps.feedback_wrong: Never update production without a database export.
steps.feedback_correct: Database saved. Update core using the minor release path.

steps.hint: Update WordPress core (minor path is fine here)
steps.output:
Updating to version 7.0.6 (en_US)...
Success: WordPress updated successfully.
steps.feedback_wrong: Database is backed up — update core next.
steps.feedback_correct: Core files updated. Sync the database schema.

steps.hint: Run the database schema update for the new core
steps.output:
Success: WordPress database already at latest db version.
Success: WordPress database upgraded successfully.
steps.feedback_wrong: After core update, always run update-db.
steps.feedback_correct: Schema is current. Update plugins next.

steps.hint: Update all plugins that have available updates
steps.output:
Enabling Maintenance mode...
Downloading update...
Unpacking the update...
Installing the latest version...
Removing the old version of the plugin...
Plugin updated successfully.
Disabling Maintenance mode...
Success: Updated 3 of 3 plugins.
steps.feedback_wrong: Update plugins with WP-CLI — not only from wp-admin.
steps.feedback_correct: Plugins updated. Confirm the updates list is empty.

steps.hint: Confirm no plugin updates are left
steps.feedback_correct: Clean updates list. Remove the risky File Manager plugin next.

steps.hint: Delete the wp-file-manager plugin from the site
accepted: wp plugin deactivate wp-file-manager && wp plugin delete wp-file-manager
steps.output:
Deleted 'wp-file-manager' plugin.
Success: Deleted 1 of 1 plugins.
steps.feedback_wrong: File Manager does not belong on production — delete it with WP-CLI.
steps.feedback_correct: Risky plugin gone. Lock installs from the dashboard.

steps.hint: Set DISALLOW_FILE_MODS so wp-admin cannot install or update plugins/themes
steps.output: Success: Added the constant 'DISALLOW_FILE_MODS' to the 'wp-config.php' file with the raw value 'true'.
steps.feedback_wrong: Use wp config set with value true, --raw, and --type=constant (name is DISALLOW_FILE_MODS).
steps.feedback_correct: Admin install path locked. Flush the cache to finish the round.

steps.feedback_wrong: Finish with a cache flush so visitors see the updated site.
steps.feedback_correct: Monthly round complete: inspected, backed up, updated, cleaned, locked, flushed.

completion.message: Nice work. You finished an entry-level monthly WP-CLI round: look → backup → update → remove risk → lock admin → flush.
completion.next_hint: Next: Secure Maintenance (premium zip + fuller hardening) or practice a files+DB backup folder outside the web root on a real server.

troubleshooting: Updating before wp db export — no undo without a backup.
Typing DISABLE_FILE_MODS — the constant is DISALLOW_FILE_MODS.
Forgetting --raw --type=constant — you may write a string instead of boolean true.
Leaving File Manager installed — high-risk browser access to files.
Assuming an empty plugin update table means core is current — still run wp core check-update.

faq.question: Why back up before updates?
faq.answer: A bad plugin or core update can break the site. A dated database export is your fast WordPress-level rollback. On real servers also archive files outside the web root.

faq.question: Minor vs major core in the check-update table?
faq.answer: Minor stays on the same series and is usually safer for a routine round. Major is a bigger jump — plan it separately with a fuller backup.

faq.question: Why delete File Manager?
faq.answer: It lets people manage server files from the browser. On production that is a common attack path if an admin account is abused.

faq.question: What does DISALLOW_FILE_MODS block?
faq.answer: Plugin and theme install/update (and the theme/plugin file editor) from wp-admin. WP-CLI on the server still works.

faq.question: Exact command to lock the admin?
faq.answer: wp config set DISALLOW_FILE_MODS true --raw --type=constant — then verify with wp config get DISALLOW_FILE_MODS.

learning_outcomes: You can read core and plugin update status with WP-CLI
You back up the database before production updates
You update core and plugins in a safe order
You remove high-risk plugins like File Manager
You lock wp-admin installs with DISALLOW_FILE_MODS using full flags
